### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via ISharingService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via ISharingService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via SharingService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce78ff7bcd850f440b2bacc25a35cedbcc847c56` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `915dc10c1774831192b2f4313a070b4c12bd3454` — the merge of head `4a6d71cfcda08d9bf78ecc959292bc516f43ee61` into base `ce78ff7bcd850f440b2bacc25a35cedbcc847c56`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 915dc10c1774831192b2f4313a070b4c12bd3454 && git checkout 915dc10c1774831192b2f4313a070b4c12bd3454
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ce78ff7bcd850f440b2bacc25a35cedbcc847c56 4a6d71cfcda08d9bf78ecc959292bc516f43ee61 && git checkout -B drift-repro ce78ff7bcd850f440b2bacc25a35cedbcc847c56 && git merge --no-ff 4a6d71cfcda08d9bf78ecc959292bc516f43ee61

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce78ff7bcd850f440b2bacc25a35cedbcc847c56
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ce78ff7bcd850f440b2bacc25a35cedbcc847c56` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9e21e91be753b7e2a3f899cc247cbd156bb1492e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22497 (body and all seven comments), PR #22535 (body, its one comment, file list), the net diff of `refs/pm/pr-22535` against its merge-base with `origin/main` (`ee8751d41e`; 4 files, +32/-16; `origin/main` is at `faf6348508`, six commits past the base), and the 46 check-runs on the head. The code each sentence describes was read at the PR head (`git show refs/pm/pr-22535:…`) and re-read at `origin/main` where that file moved.

### ① Derived judgments

Every hunk in the diff is inside a `/** … */` block or the new changeset. No accept-set changes: no Zod schema, no type alias member, no export, no runtime line moves. The public-surface changes are TSDoc on four published docblocks, judged one by one against the code at this head:

1. **`ControlledByParentWriteDenialLeg`, `master_chain` bullet — RIGHT.** `SecurityPlugin.assertControlledByParentWrite` (`security-plugin.ts:9263`) loops from the record's own master: iteration one runs `assertMasterRowEditable(permissionSets, hopRel = rel, hopMasterId = masterId, …)` (:9473), then sets `masterObject = hopRel.master` (:9477), which is that same master. When `declaresControlledByParent(masterObject)` holds (:9478), the no-relation (:9496–:9503), row-not-present (:9507–:9515) and empty-master-reference (:9516–:9523) refusals all throw `masterEditDenied('master_chain', …)` naming `masterObject`; the cycle (:9480) and depth-bound (:9488) refusals are `master_chain` too. So "a master that is itself `controlled_by_parent` (the record's own master, or any master above it)" is what the code decides. The adjacent frame "Past the record itself the check answers these as refusals, not as defects of the request" is also right: for the addressed record the same three conditions throw `MasterDetailRelationMissingError` (:9306), `DetailRecordNotFoundError` (:9321) and `MasterReferenceMissingError` (:9459), which `controlledByParentWriteOutcomeOf` maps to `unresolvable`; from the first master on they are the `master_chain` leg. The dev's four-word deviation ("Above the first hop" to "Past the record itself") is required by the first sentence, not optional.

2. **`ControlledByParentWriteUnresolvedReason`, `record_not_found` bullet — RIGHT.** "This is the addressed record, not its master": `DetailRecordNotFoundError` is thrown only at :9321, for `(object, targetId)`. Where the master governs its own rows the loop breaks at :9478 right after the legs, and nothing reads that master row for existence — only the row-level-security leg's `findOne` under the master write filter and the record-sharing leg see it, and they judge it as any row (they may pass; the sentence claims nothing stronger). Where the master is itself `controlled_by_parent`, `readRowById(masterObject, hopMasterId)` at :9507 runs after `assertMasterRowEditable` on every iteration, the first included, and an absent row is `master_chain`. "after the legs" correctly leaves the floor-constrained case (a leg refusing first) unclaimed; the dev declared it NOT MEASURED, and the sentence does not need it.

3. **`ISharingService.canEdit`, write-depth paragraph — RIGHT.** At the head `comment-access-hooks.ts:422` calls `sharing.checkEdit(target.object, target.recordId, callerCtx)` and `attachment-access-hooks.ts:402` calls `sharing.checkEdit(object, String(recordId), callerCtx)`; both type the dependency as a `Pick` of `ISharingService` on `checkEdit` alone (:137, :106) and neither calls `canEdit`. The retained clause "matches ownership at `own`" still holds through `checkEdit`: both `callerContext` helpers strip the operation-private keys (`withoutOperationPrivateKeys`), so no `__writeScope` reaches `checkEdit` and `resolveOwnerScopeIds(context, undefined)` matches at `own`.

4. **`ISharingService.canEdit` two-state caller list and `SharingService.canEdit` caller list — RIGHT as to the removal.** `canEdit` callers at the head outside tests: `sharing-plugin.ts:1263` (the sharing middleware), `security-plugin.ts:5638` (`resolveSharingCanEdit`, the ADR-0055 master check's sharing leg) and `security-plugin.ts:5526` (explain's `canEditRecord` binding). The two parent gates are no longer callers, so dropping them is right, and the two names kept are the two gating callers. Explain's binding is a reporter, not a gate that "ADDS this gate to whatever else guards the row"; its omission predates this PR and sits in the acceptance notes. Not a misstatement.

5. **Changeset text — RIGHT, one compression noted.** "Each names the master whose own master the walk could not derive" and "Those gates read `checkEdit` and the master-detail write check" (`checkControlledByParentWrite` at comment :448, attachment :428) both hold; "keep their declared shapes" holds since no type or code line moves. The compression: "the legs judge a missing row only where the master governs its own rows" — the legs run on every hop before the row read, so a leg can refuse a missing `controlled_by_parent` master row first (the unmeasured floor case). The docblock's "after the legs" is the contract and states it precisely; the CHANGELOG sentence reads as the common case. Not a contract misstatement.

6. **Against current `main`.** Of the files these sentences describe, only `security-plugin.ts` moved in the six commits past the base (`d303b3e7af`, PR #22529: explain's update verdict now also asks `checkControlledByParentWrite`, and the pre-image floor vouch). The walk and `assertMasterRowEditable` are unchanged; the `canEdit` caller set at `faf6348508` is the same three sites; both hooks are unchanged. Every sentence holds at `main` as well as at the base.

### ② Semver level

The diff publishes in exactly two packages, and each has its own entry in `.changeset/22497-master-chain-docblock.md`:

- `@objectstack/spec` `patch` — right. `files[]` ships `dist`; `src/contracts/index.ts` re-exports `security-service` and `sharing-service`; tsup emits `dts`, so the three edited spec docblocks ship in `dist/contracts/index.d.ts`. TSDoc only; no export, authorable key or behaviour change, so `patch` is the floor and nothing reaches `minor`.
- `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` `patch` — right. `files[]` ships `dist`; `index.ts` exports `SharingService`; its build is the root tsup config plus `check-dts-emitted.mjs`, so the edited `SharingService.canEdit` docblock ships in `dist/index.d.ts`. Same reasoning. (Both packages sit in the `fixed` group, so they version together regardless; the entry is still owed and present.)

No third package is touched. `Clause-②: no` appears in the changeset body and on PR body line 3 — right: no new key on any published payload, so no `minor` is owed and `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` do not apply. Not `skip-changeset`: both packages publish the text. `Check Changeset` (three runs) and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries the changeset gates: ADR-0087 registration, no-major / level axis, empty-changeset) are green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

**`open_questions`:** `[]` in both os-dev reports (6088993530, 6089641316). Nothing to answer.

**Dev deviations, each answered:**
1. "Above the first hop" to "Past the record itself": required by the first sentence; right (①.1).
2. `ISharingService.canEdit` edited in two sentences: both are the same caller-list claim; right (①.3, ①.4).
3. Changeset headline "three" to "four": matches the diff, four docblocks across two files; right.
4. No merge of `origin/main` into the branch: the check-runs ran on the merge of this head into `faf6348508` (per the Docs Drift comment's tree line), the six commits falsify no sentence (①.6), and the queue rebuilds on landing. Acceptable.
5. The surface widened by one bullet on seat order 6089034303: same file, same first-hop misstatement class, the ordered sentence landed verbatim; right (①.2).
6. PR assignee unset (the dev's `label-write --assign` was refused by its classifier and not retried by another route): a process residue the owning seat holds per 6089680436; not a contract matter and not a reviewer write.
7. The unquoted-heredoc incident (an unlocked spec build, `check:i18n`, two prerequisite-refused gates, a whole-repo lint terminated by recorded PID): the dev reports a clean tree afterwards, the three commits on the branch are exactly the diff read here, and none of those runs is cited as evidence. Recorded on the card; no effect on the contract.
8. Contracts tests, plugin-sharing build/typecheck and the rosters carried over from `99f06a1073` rather than re-run at the head: `Test Core` (six shards), `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates` ran on this head and are green, which is the verdict that counts.

**`out_of_scope_findings`, each dispositioned:**
- The `record_not_found` bullet: resolved in this PR (①.2).
- `controlled-by-parent-write-member.test.ts:306` is titled for a master above the record's own master while its fixture is the first-hop case; the assertion is right. Neither a reproducible defect, a contract violation nor an authoring trap, so the acceptance note is the right carrier (Prime Directive #10). Not escalated.
- Explain's `canEditRecord` unnamed in the two `canEdit` caller lists: pre-existing; a reporter, not a gate (①.4). Acceptance note; not escalated.
- `permission-evaluator.ts:369`, `explain-engine.ts:1950` and `attachments-fixture.ts:15` comments still name the attachment gate as a `canEdit` consumer: code comments with no runtime reader, outside the docblocks the card names. Acceptance note; not escalated.

**The red check on this head.** 46 check-runs; every required context is green except `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` (job 114021328084, run 37989816695), `failure` at step 2 `Initialize containers`: `docker pull postgres:16` answered `toomanyrequests: You have reached your unauthenticated pull rate limit` three times with back-off, then `Docker pull failed with exit code 1`. Step 3 `Checkout repository` and every build and test step after it were skipped. **The failure does not reach this PR's change**: no source was checked out and no test body ran; it is a runner-side Docker Hub pull fault, which the seat's acceptance on the card (6089680436) names as p0 #22541. It is still one of the seven required contexts, so landing needs a green run of that job on this head or on a `main`-merged head — a landing condition for the owning seat, not a contract finding.

**Governance and size.** None of the four paths is a governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); this record is the compensating control the dispatch owes on the `packages/spec/src/**` limb. 48 changed lines, under the 3,000-line human-merge threshold; head repo is the base repo.
